Claim with `./hq claim 113 --agent claude`, build strictly inside the issue's Scope, run `./hq check`, rebase on origin/main, open the PR with `./hq pr 113 --body-file .context/pr-113.md`, then stop and report PR number and evidence. 1	---
2	name: hq-work
3	description: 'Use when a human assigns you a GitHub issue ("work on #N" or "/hq-work N"). Takes it from claim to a reviewed PR.'
4	---
5	
6	# hq-work
7	
8	`N` = issue, `<you>` = `claude`, `codex` or `cursor`, `<PR>` = PR number. Windows: `hq.cmd` for `./hq`.
9	
10	1. Claim: `./hq claim N --agent <you>`. If it refuses, stop and tell the human why. Read what it
11	   prints: the issue, work in flight, overlapping files.
12	2. Context before code. Read only the docs the issue needs, then run
13	   `entire search "<topic>"`, `entire graph query "<task>"` and `entire brain brief "<task>"`.
14	   Before rewriting code you did not write: `entire why <file>:<line>`.
15	3. Plan inline in a few bullets. No spec or plan documents.
16	4. Build inside Scope, never in "Do not touch". Small commits, staged by name:
17	   `git add <file> <file> && git commit -m "<what the product can now do>"`.
18	   Push whenever you like: `git push -u origin HEAD`.
19	5. Verify: run the issue's Verify steps, then `./hq check` until it passes.
20	6. Sync with main. Not pushed yet: `git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main`. Already pushed:
21	   `git fetch origin && git merge origin/main` (never force-push). Fix conflicts in your own
22	   changes, `git add <files>`, then `git rebase --continue` or `git commit`. Re-run `./hq check`.
23	7. Write `.context/pr-N.md` (template below; `mkdir -p .context` if needed), then
24	   `./hq pr N --body-file .context/pr-N.md`. It pushes, opens the PR with `Closes #N` and sets
25	   `status:review`. Get the number: `gh pr view --json number,url`.
26	8. Trail: Entire opens a trail for your PR by itself. Check it with `entire trail show`, then run `entire trail ci-pr` (safe to re-run). Only if `trail show` finds none: `entire trail create --title "<issue title> (#N)" --type feature`.
27	9. Review, unless the issue is `size:S`: `entire review`. Fix real findings, commit, `git push`,
28	   re-run `./hq check`. Then `gh pr edit <PR> --add-label review:pass` and `entire trail ready`.
29	10. Report the PR link, check result and risks, then stop. Merge only on "ship it" (`/hq-ship`).
30	
31	PR body template for `.context/pr-N.md`:
32	
33	````markdown
34	## What changed
35	- <what the product can now do>
36	
37	## How verified
38	- <Verify steps you ran and what you saw>
39	```
40	<tail of ./hq check>
41	```
42	
43	## Risks
44	- <what could break, or "none">
45	
46	## Screenshots
47	<UI changes only, else "n/a">
48	````
49	
50	Out of scope: do not do it. Write `.context/new-issue.md` with the headings `### Goal`,
51	`### Acceptance criteria`, `### Scope`, `### Do not touch`, `### Blocked by`, `### Verify`,
52	`### Notes` (say "Found while working on #N" in Notes), then
53	`gh issue create --title "<title>" --body-file .context/new-issue.md --label status:needs-human`.
54	Link it on your issue: `gh issue comment N --body "Follow-up: #M"`. Carry on with your own scope.
55	
56	Stuck (unclear criteria, waiting on another issue, a conflict in code you did not write):
57	`./hq release N --needs-human --note "<one crisp question>"`, then stop.
58	
59	Done means: every acceptance criterion met, `./hq check` passes with its tail in the PR, PR open
60	with evidence, `review:pass` (unless `size:S`).

### Goal

The roadworks map can retrieve permit geometry, dates and schedule confidence from the works API.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Define and export a typed `works.near` result with permit reference, GeoJSON LineString/Polygon when supplied, representative Point fallback only when no extent exists, and a location-precision flag.
- [ ] Include proposed and actual dates when known, scheduled night-work status, and an explicit unknown-schedule state; do not infer that a permit is an observed noise event.
- [ ] Implement `works.near` from stored Street Manager permits with bounded radius and date filters; distinguish absent geometry from malformed geometry.
- [ ] Cover a real extent, point fallback, unknown schedule and out-of-range coordinates with fixtures and tests.
- [ ] Do not add building or demolition sites that Street Manager does not cover.

### Scope

- `packages/shared/src/works/`
- `apps/server/src/features/works/`

### Do not touch

Other feature folders, registries, `apps/mobile/src/lib/`, integrations, database shared code, `packages/shared/src/domain/`, and root configuration.

### Blocked by

#66

### Verify

- `bun test packages/shared/src/works apps/server/src/features/works`
- `./hq check`

### Notes

- This is a dedicated API contract issue. The works map UI follows after this result is stable.
- Read `docs/DOMAIN.md: Street Manager` and its wording rules. Scheduled night work differs from a classified construction sound outside the council's recommended hours.

content.thinking:
I'm weighing whether to keep the stored WorkRecord as is and add a new response type, WorkNearItem, since the stored geometry is always a non-null Point or LineString with no flag showing whether it's a fallback. I'm also considering an optional stored field, geometryPrecision, to tell absent geometry apart from malformed geometry, and I note that adding it to the shared works is in scope.

I'm settling on how to tell absent geometry from malformed geometry: a bad WKT string that triggers the fallback counts as malformed, and since the integration requires a non-empty WKT, a missing value isn't a real case. I'm leaning toward a single optional stored `geometryStatus` field, and I'm also checking whether out-of-range coordinates should be treated as malformed too.

I'm sketching out the shape of the result: a `worksNearItem` carrying the permit and work reference numbers, street, category, authority, geometry with a location precision, a status field for geometry, proposed and actual start and end dates, and a night-work flag that can be scheduled, not scheduled, or unknown. The unknown case applies when there are no proposed clock times and the traffic management type doesn't indicate night work, while a known time without night work counts as not scheduled. The stored record stays as it is, with only the optional geometry status added, and the nearby results are built by mapping each record into one of these items.

I'm now checking how the existing tests use `result.works`, whether they treat it as raw records, and whether any mobile code consumes it.

content.thinking:
I'm sorting out how to classify stored geometry at read time, since integration already rejects malformed WKT and only corrupted storage could produce it. My thinking is that a valid stored extent counts as an extent, and a stored point is the supplied location, so it should be marked with precision "point" rather than treated as a representative fallback.

I'm settling on a simple rule: extents (LineString and Polygon) get precision "extent", and a stored Point gets "point". Missing or null geometry is the open question, since there'd be no representative point to fall back on. I'll keep the change contained to the server's works folder, with the repo reading stored records tolerantly instead of letting one malformed document fail the whole request, and I'm planning the shared types and helpers around that.

I'm weighing how to report geometry that is missing versus malformed, since the Mongo query only ever returns documents that have geometry. A classifier that sorts each raw record into ok, absent, or malformed (with out-of-range coordinates counted as malformed) feels like the cleanest approach, with the query tallying the excluded ones. That means the repo should hand back loosely typed records rather than throwing on bad parses.

I'm going to parse the stored documents without the geometry field first, then attach the raw geometry separately so a malformed shape doesn't break the whole read. The in-memory repo's distance check would also fail on bad geometry, so it needs a guard. Next I'll check how the existing repo tests use findNear, since they may expect fully typed records back.

# claude-code review

Request changes: the new `omitted` counts can only be non-zero in tests. The Mongo `$near` query never returns permits that have no geometry or bad geometry, so in production the map is always told nothing was left off.

Effort was medium, carried over from your last review. I didn't run the tests or the type-checker.

- [medium] `apps/server/src/features/works/query.ts:18` and `apps/server/src/features/works/repo.ts:147`: `worksNear` counts `absentGeometry` and `malformedGeometry` from what `findNear` returns. The Mongo repository uses `$near` on the `works.geometry` 2dsphere index (`apps/server/src/db/indexes.ts:10`). That query only matches documents with a valid, indexed geometry, so permits with missing or bad geometry never come back. Production therefore always gets `omitted: {absentGeometry: 0, malformedGeometry: 0}`, and the map will say no permits were left out when some were. The only test that exercises `omitted` injects a fake `findNear` that returns broken rows, which Mongo cannot do. Fix: count these permits with their own query (for example `geometry: {$exists: false}` within the area), or drop `omitted` and enforce valid geometry when permits are written.
- [low] `apps/server/src/features/works/repo.ts:54`: for a Polygon, `distanceToWork` only checks the outer ring `coordinates[0]`. A point inside a hole gets distance 0, and the distance to the hole's edge is never measured. Any polygon with holes reports too-close distances inside the holes. Fix: return 0 only when the point is inside the outer ring and outside every hole. The edge loop already covers all rings.
- [low] `packages/shared/src/works/index.ts:25`: the stricter `position` check (finite numbers, valid lon/lat ranges) is also inside `workRecord`, which `permitToWork` parses (`apps/server/src/features/works/document.ts:65`). Before, an out-of-range point from the BNG conversion or the fallback point would just be stored. Now `storePermit` throws. Nothing is classified as "malformed", and the incoming permit is rejected inside `receiveStreetManagerPost`. Fix: catch the parse failure in `geometryFromPermit` or `storePermit` and return a reason, or drop the permit, rather than throwing.
- [low] `packages/shared/src/works/index.ts:65`: the `workRecord` doc comment still says it is "returned by `works.near`". `works.near` now returns `worksNearItem`, which has a different `nightWork` type (an enum, not a boolean) and no `eventType` or `objectReference`. A client written from this comment would read `nightWork` as a boolean, and since the string `"not_scheduled"` is truthy it would count as night work. Fix: change the comment to say `works.near` returns `worksNearItem`.
